user_stories.story: As a user, when I open the page I see all existing logs, newest first, without doing anything.
As a user, I see each log's description, its date in a readable local format, and its photos.
As a user with no logs, I see the empty message.
As a user, if loading fails, I see a visible error instead of a blank page.
As a user, photos actually load because the server serves the uploads directory at /uploads/.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: On page load (GET /), app.js issues exactly one GET /api/logs (observable in the network log or a request-counting stub server) without any user interaction.

With N logs in the DB, #log-list contains exactly N li.log elements, cloned from #log-template, in the same order as the API response (newest first). The template element itself is unchanged and no li is rendered when N=0.

Each li.log's p.log-description textContent equals the log's description exactly. A description such as x appears as literal text: no b/img child elements are created in the description, and no script runs/dialog appears.

Each li.log's time.log-date has a datetime attribute equal to the log's created_at string verbatim, and visible text that is a non-empty human-readable local date/time (not the raw ISO string) corresponding to that instant.

Each log's div.log-photos contains one img per entry in photos, in order, with a src that resolves to /uploads/<filename> on the same origin (e.g. img.src ends with /uploads/<uuid>.<ext>, not /uploads/uploads/... or /static/...). In a real browser each such img finishes loading (complete is true and naturalWidth > 0 for a valid image). A log with zero photos has no img elements.
When the API returns an empty list, #empty-message is visible (hidden attribute removed) and #log-list has no items. When logs exist, #empty-message stays hidden.

When GET /api/logs fails (non-2xx status or network error/unparseable body), a visible error message element with non-empty text is shown on the page, #empty-message is not shown as if there were no logs, and no uncaught exception is the only signal. The error is not shown on success.

Backend: a photo uploaded via POST /api/logs is retrievable with GET /uploads/<filename> returning 200 with bytes identical to the upload and an image content-type, using the uploads_dir passed to create_app (including a non-default tmp dir in tests).

Traversal is refused: requests such as /uploads/../<file outside uploads dir>, /uploads/%2e%2e/..., /uploads/..%2f..., and an encoded absolute path never return the content of a file outside the uploads directory (response is 4xx, verified with a sentinel file placed beside the uploads dir). The uploads directory listing itself is not exposed (GET /uploads/ is not 200 with a listing).
Existing behaviour is intact: GET / still returns index.html, /static/ still serves frontend files, POST/GET /api/logs unchanged, and all 55 existing tests plus the new tests pass.

Edits are limited to frontend/app.js, backend/main.py, backend/tests/test_logs.py (index.html only if needed for an error element; models.py only for a constant). No new files. style.css, docs and Docker untouched. After tests, the project contains no stray DB, uploads files, __pycache__ or .pytest_cache.

app.js is plain JavaScript with no libraries or build step, and does not use innerHTML (or equivalent) with user-supplied data. Edit/Delete buttons are rendered in each log but have no behavior; the create form is not wired.

assumptions.assumption: photos in the API are "uploads/<file>" (relative, no leading slash); the frontend must turn them into a same-origin absolute path "/uploads/<file>" so it works regardless of page URL.
Error display uses either a new element created by app.js or a minimal addition to index.html; the implementer chooses, provided it is visible and does not depend on style.css (empty).
"Readable local format" means any locale-formatted date/time via the browser's built-in facilities; exact format is not tested beyond being non-ISO and non-empty.
created_at is a UTC ISO string possibly lacking an explicit offset; the displayed local time must treat it as UTC.
The error message should also clear/replace on re-render; since there is no retry in this stage, a single load attempt is enough.
Photo img elements get an alt attribute (e.g. generic text); not tested.

edge_cases.case: Description containing HTML, quotes, ampersands, newlines, or very long unbroken text.
Log with zero photos; log with several photos.
created_at without a trailing Z or offset (must still be read as UTC); invalid date string should not crash the render of other logs.
Empty list vs. failed request are distinct states.
Filenames with unusual characters should be URL-safe in src.
Traversal variants: raw .., percent-encoded .., backslash forms (Windows host), absolute paths, symlinks/junctions leading out of the directory.
Uploads directory not existing at app creation time (should not crash app startup or break other routes).
Backend serving /uploads must not shadow /api or /static routes.

risks.risk: Windows path handling may let backslash or drive-letter traversal slip past naive checks; tests must cover these.
Mounting a static file handler at create_app time when uploads_dir is created lazily or later could fail or serve a stale path.
Treating a timezone-less ISO timestamp as local time shows the wrong time.
Verifier needs a real image to confirm naturalWidth > 0; a stub non-image file would load as broken.

dependencies.dependency: Existing backend (create_app, routes, models, database) and its web framework's static-file facilities, with no new packages if avoidable.
frontend/index.html element ids: log-list, empty-message, log-template and its inner classes.
Browser fetch/DOM APIs; a real browser or headless page for the UI criteria.

spec.self_critique: Every story maps to criteria: load/order (1,2), description/date/photos (3-5), empty (6), error (7), serving (8-10). Criteria 1-7 are checkable in a headless browser against a running app; 8-11 via the test suite. The biggest risk is traversal behavior on Windows and the exact definition of "visible error" without CSS; both are specified by observable outcomes rather than mechanisms. No blocking ambiguity remained.
